fieldNotes.locating: Roster coords (40.171509, -85.766582) landed in farmland ~15 km NW of the plant. Web research established the Nestlé beverage factory + DC is south of Anderson along I-69 (a.k.a. 4301 W 450 S / 4301 W 73rd St). The correct building - a ~1.1M sq ft multi-section plant with milk/liquid storage tanks on the NE and large trailer drop yards on the W - was located at approximately 40.0382, -85.7440 ('I-69/Hwy 38 west of exit 222, north side', per the Nesquik Bunny landmark). Locked center 40.03820, -85.74400.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Modern (2008-built, $359M) Nestlé beverage factory + distribution center on a fully private campus with a perimeter road loop, surrounded by buffer land, ponds and farmland. A controlled, guarded truck gate is near-certain for a food-grade beverage plant + DC of this scale; the truck flow enters from the W side. The exact barrier arm could not be isolated in satellite imagery and there is no public Street View reaching the entrance, so flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth positively confirmed in available overhead imagery; classified guardShack false with remoteGs true (kiosk / app check-in) as the conservative read - low confidence on the pair.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Large dock banks on the W and SW building faces with many trailers backed in; estimated 50+ doors across faces - banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very large trailer drop yards on the W and SW: multiple long rows holding well over 150 trailers in the captured imagery - clearly 50+.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated large trailer-storage lots, separate from the active dock aprons.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock clusters on the W (DC/distribution) and SW (factory) faces suggest physically separate ship/receive operations - medium confidence.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons and a private road loop with ample width give clear room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur runs into the property; the plant is entirely truck-served.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: South of Anderson along I-69 amid farmland and an edge-of-metro industrial park; per rubric, classified Rural (open-country/edge setting).
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from perimeter box (~850m N-S x ~800m E-W) ~ 80 acres for the campus footprint.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main factory/DC building plus an ancillary structure; effectively a combined factory + distribution center under one campus.
